claim: The research loop is closed at the artifact level but its intake is vocabulary-shaped: zero-hit questions are correct AND-semantics, not a bug, and the corpus's own boundary condition ('the vocabulary must be maintained, or questions silently go unanswered') is currently unmonitored — dead_route_tags() checks prompt tags, not question reachability.
bet: Add scripts/check_reachability.py seeded with this session's own zero-hit runs ('speculation horizon reality', 'verification negative control', 'idea inbox capture') plus known-good controls; exit 1 if any seeded question reaches zero chunks. Falsifiable: a topics.md alias that makes all seeded questions hit passes the gate; a still-unreachable question names a real vocabulary gap.

claim: A plan with a bigger horizon is based more on speculation, so the next step must be based on reality the most. A subpar plan hurts more than no plan at all, plan influence decays with context-window pressure (distance IS horizon), and intrinsic self-correction actively degrades performance — so far phases can only be validated by the planner's own anticipation, while the near step is validated by the environment. Detail density should be inversely proportional to horizon: a step beyond the next gateable artifact is a bet, not a procedure.
bet: Add a `basis:` column to the five phase rows of pipeline/WORKFLOW.md classifying each as environment-validated / artifact-validated / anticipation-only, plus one Compliance sentence: specification detail is inversely proportional to horizon. Falsifiable: a later reflection cites the column and exhibits a far phase carrying procedure-level detail — that citation is the now-detectable violation.

claim: Task division is already HTN-shaped and one-level adaptive, but route.py's ADAPT split triggers on cardinality (card < threshold) while ADAPT triggers on the executor's observed inability. The proxy is wrong in the case that matters: a route returning many wrong chunks never triggers a split. Chief-of-staff routing's cost model requires the classifier to have visibility into downstream capability, which a cardinality proxy lacks.
bet: Extend route.py --json with a split_signal field reading the last digest's citation-resolution result for the topic; split one level on failure signal instead of on card < threshold. Falsifiable: route the same topic before and after — the id set must change only when the prior digest failed; changing on cardinality alone means the trigger is still the proxy and the bet failed.

claim: The reflection process has the external grounding channel (citations must resolve in graph.db) and the eviction mechanism (phase 5) but not the third requirement: the diagnosis is composed, not extracted. Honest Lying's mitigation is to replace open-ended self-diagnosis with programmatic extraction of trajectory-level failure signals — the environment, not the agent's reasoning, supplies the error content (correct-object mention 0% -> 86%, RRR 0.64 -> 0.10). Separately, candidates have no contrast source, though ExpeL's insights come from failed-vs-successful contrasts, and the claim/evidence/bet schema has no condition field though grounding and abstraction are orthogonal axes.
bet: Add a gate line to check_reflection.py rejecting any candidate whose `bet` field contains no path-shaped token (a /-separated path or script name), plus a `contrast` field recording what the lesson was contrasted against. Falsifiable: write one candidate with a prose-only bet — it must fail. That negative control is the proof, mirroring this project's own R3 (validate a contract with its negative controls, not the happy path).

claim: Problem monitoring is the strongest area because every defect was found by testing the invariant the pipeline claims rather than auditing for tidiness — but the postmortem lessons live as unqueryable prose in reflection/2026-*.md, which is exactly the failure the corpus names ('a closed family written only in prose is closed to a careful reader and open to everyone else'). The recurring defect class is a monitor that silently passes: the manifest gate crashed on every ingest while ingest.py exited 0, and a gate that regenerates its subject cannot detect that the subject is wrong (240 of 596 chunks attributed to phantom provenance while passing).
bet: Add a check_postmortem_rule.py sub-gate asserting every reflection/2026-*.md postmortem carries an R1 prevention rule naming an owning file. Falsifiable: run against the six existing postmortems — if all conform the gate is free and its value lands on the seventh; if any lacks a routed rule, the gate caught a real gap on its first run.

claim: Knowledge storing is the most completely built area and the corpus validates the build directly — the three layers (folder vocabulary / lossless corpus / graph index) are the configuration the benchmark does not test: lossless write plus supplementary query-shaped index. The gap is that injection is one-directional: GRAPH-DIGEST.md is auto-injected into the reflection agent but accepted candidates are not on any read path a future working agent reads by default. The corpus measured this: near-perfect LoCoMo models drop to 40-60% in MemoryArena — passive recall is not decision-relevant use.
bet: Wire scripts/promote_candidate.py so an accepted candidate appends its one-line rule (with evidence chunk id) to a single rules file already listed as an input in stages/04_reflect/CONTEXT.md. Falsifiable: after promotion, ask.py for the rule's topic must return the rule's chunk id; if it does not, the promotion never reached the read path and the loop is still open.

claim: The graph is fast and deterministic because it refuses to be smart — content-addressed identity means the query path needs no LLM and a recursive CTE walks k hops in 2 ms with a ~400-token injection fixed at any corpus size. The real risk to that property is not query cost but index inflation silently degrading the one consumer: the project already shipped 1.6M edges for 177k relationships, one node carrying 4,527 edges, and a one-hop expansion returning 15,190 rows collapsing to 594 distinct neighbors — 90.7% of edges from tags selecting over 25% of the corpus. The fix was applied once by hand; the invariant preventing its return is not checked.
bet: Add a check_graph_economy.py build-time gate (or build_graph.py --report) emitting per-tag selectivity and edge share, failing when any single tag accounts for over 25% of edges. Falsifiable: run on the current 633-node graph — passing means the hand fix held; a flagged tag means the inflation returned. This applies the corpus's own rule (record magnitude, not verdict) to the graph itself.

claim: The unified graph brain is not one graph and not a router-of-routers: one-level routing is the measured optimum and a second deeper routing level never helped and sometimes broke accuracy outright. The correct reading of 'unified' is unified identity and closed vocabulary over federated stores — one content-addressed id space shared across sub-brains so a citation from another brain resolves, while each brain owns its store, fingerprint, and eviction. Federation by auto-merge is the exact 43-side-copy failure the four-moves protocol exists to prevent.
bet: Write one file, knowledge/IDENTITY.md, declaring the id rule (content-addressed, id == filename stem), the shared vocabulary pointer (knowledge/topics.md), and the federation rule (each brain owns its store + fingerprint + eviction; ids cross-resolve; nothing is auto-merged). Falsifiable: a second brain cites a workspace-research chunk id and it resolves — the one assertion federation depends on; if it does not resolve, the vocabulary is not actually shared and the dream is still one graph.

claim: The reflection_brain scar 'diagnostics live in logs, lessons live in MONITORING/reflection/' is contradicted by the corpus: a prose-recorded lesson is closed to a careful reader and open to everyone else, so the logs/prose split is precisely what leaves the lesson unqueryable. The prior scars are otherwise confirmed: a problem is solved only at systematic_fix_applied (a routed invariant, not a recorded verdict), and no plan or diagnosis starts without the Prior-Knowledge Check — the retrieval side of the reality-weighted gradient.
bet: Route one prevention rule from each existing postmortem into the gated candidate ledger (reflection/candidates/*.jsonl) so it becomes subject to evidence grounding and phase-5 eviction instead of prose. Falsifiable: the routed rule must survive check_reflection.py with a resolving evidence id; a rule whose evidence id no longer resolves is evicted rather than left as prose that silently describes a graph that no longer exists.

claim: Across all eight focus areas the project closes the loop at the artifact level and leaves it open at the read level: it builds, gates, and evicts, but does not guarantee that what it validated is what the next agent actually reads. The corpus measured this asymmetry precisely — retrieval method moved accuracy 14-23 points against write strategy's 3-8 with precision predicting accuracy at r = 0.98, and near-perfect recall models drop to 40-60% when memory must be used decision-relevantly rather than passively recalled.
bet: A single gate, scripts/check_reachability.py, asserting (a) every question the working agent is expected to ask reaches at least one chunk and (b) every accepted candidate's evidence id is on a read path the working agent actually reads. Falsifiable: exit 0 means the read loop is closed and the next bet is the WORKFLOW.md basis column; exit 1 names the gap — the two conditions the corpus says are silent today are an unanswered question and a validated lesson nobody reads.
